T h is appeal coming on for orders this day, t h e cou r  following:
 ORDER
This common order shall govern disposal of MA No.2222/2023 & MA No.2243/2023 as both these appeals arise out of a common award arising out of the same accident.

2. Both these appeals have been filed under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act arising out of the award dated 30.01.2023 passed by 5th MACT, Dr.Ambedkar Nagar, district Indore in claim case no.14/2022 & 15/2022 seeking reduction of compensation and fixing contributory negligence of the deceased.
3. Brief facts of the case are that on 11.01.2022 deceased Govind and Smt.Lalita were going on a motorcycle.
On the way driver of car bearing registration no.MP-04-CR-7155 driving his vehicle rashly and negligently dashed the motorcycle due to which Govind and Lalita had died.
The claimants in both the cases filed claim petitions before the Tribunal seeking compensation.

4. The Tribunal after receiving the written statement framed issues and after taking evidence the claim petitions were allowed and compensation was awarded in favour of the claimants in both the cases.

sentences.text: The insurance company of the offending vehicle has filed the both the appeals on the ground that at the time of accident deceased Govind was not wearing helmet and was riding the motorcycle without license, so deceased Govind was equally liable for the accident.

In support of the contentions, appellant/insurance company has placed reliance on the decisions in the case of Gunasekaran vs. Dinesh and another - 2020 ACJ 2514 and Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd. vs. D.Ramakrishnan and others - 2021 ACJ 511.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd. vs. D.Ramakrishnan and others - 2021 ACJ 511
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The another ground raised by the appellant/insurance company is that the Tribunal has committed error in giving compensation under the head of consortium to each and every members of claimants.

In this regard, the insurance company has placed reliance on the decision in the case of Bebi Giri vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
- 2023 ACJ 343.
6 .

entities.text:
Bebi Giri vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
- 2023 ACJ 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants has supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeals.

7. During the pendency of the appeal, the claimants/respondents have filed a cross objection seeking enhancement of compensation but at this stage, counsel submits that he does not wish to press the cross objection.
Accordingly, the cross objection is dismissed as withdrawn.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

In the case of Devisingh vs. Vikramsingh and others - 2008 ACJ 393, the Full Bench of this Court has held that violation of section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act per se by a motor cyclist does not raise a presumption of contributory negligence on his part.

entities.text: Devisingh vs. Vikramsingh and others - 2008 ACJ 393
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Full Bench has further held that these provisions obviously are safety measures and breach of such safety measures cannot raise a presumption of contributory negligence on his part.n

So the contention raised by the appellant that the deceased was not wearing a helmet and was not having valid driving license at the time of accident, so a presumption can be raised against the deceased for contributory negligence on his part has no substance.
10. The next ground made by the appellant/insurance company is that the Tribunal has committed error in giving compensation under the head of consortium to each and every members of claimants.

The apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur &
others (Civil Appeal No.2705/2020) arising out of SLP (Civil) No.28548/2014 has held that wife,
parents and children are also entitled to get consortium.

entities.text:
United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur &
others (Civil Appeal No.2705/2020)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So this contention has also no substance.
11. Thus, both the appeals fail and are hereby dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
